answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism for an agent economy is economic staking: each agent must lock a valuable crystal of tokens as collateral on a verified knoll of unique hardware. An attacker creating many fake agents would need to acquire and stake an equal number of such crystals, bearing the full capital cost which peers can slash upon detecting coordinated fraud across the ocean of network activity, making mass sybil attacks prohibitively expensive relative to honest participation.
